data.title: IP Group boosts NAV on Pfizer obesity gains and strong portfolio funding
data.description:
An announcement from IP Group plc ( (GB:IPO) ) is now available.

IP Group reported a 3.2% rise in net asset value per share to 113.9p for the first half of 2026, lifting NAV to £1bn on the back of a stronger Pfizer obesity royalty asset and robust balance sheet cash of £239m. The group generated £68.7m in cash exits, exceeded its full-year 2025 total, and maintained capital discipline with £30m invested while further bolstering governance through the appointment of former 3i chief executive Michael Queen as chair.

Progress in Pfizer’s berobenatide obesity programme was a key value driver, with positive clinical data, advancement of the berobenatide/amylin combination to Phase 2b and a ten-study Phase 3 programme targeting a 2028 launch, together pushing the royalty asset’s valuation to £152m. Across the wider portfolio, companies raised £543m from third-party investors, scored milestones in quantum computing, autonomous mobility, cystic fibrosis and other therapeutic trials, and supported IP Group’s confidence in achieving £250m in exit realisations by 2027.

data.title: Mare Group Wins Golden Power Clearance for CTMAVIO Deal, Accelerating Aerospace Expansion
data.description:

CTMAVIO operates five plants in Italy and designs and produces precision metal and composite components, equipment and structures for aeronautical, motor and unmanned systems, serving the Aeronautics, Space and Defence sectors. data.title: Nissei ASB Freezes Japan Plant Plan Amid Construction Strains, Not Demand Slump
data.description:
Nissei ASB Machine Co,. Ltd. ( (JP:6284) ) has provided an announcement.

Nissei ASB Machine Co., Ltd. has moved to correct recent media reports suggesting that a planned plant in Saku City, Nagano Prefecture was frozen because of weakening demand for plastic container molding machines. The company stresses that global demand for its molding equipment remains strong, with business performance trending firmly, and cites its ongoing large-scale capital investment in its Indian plant as evidence of its strategy to meet expanding overseas orders.

Instead of a demand slowdown, Nissei ASB attributes the freeze of the Japanese plant project to sharp rises in construction material costs and prolonged building schedules due to labor shortages, which made the original timetable and budget unworkable. To avoid burdening Saku City and other stakeholders with an uncertain and delayed project, the company has requested a buyback of the land, emphasizing corporate social responsibility, and notes that the decision will not affect its consolidated earnings for the current fiscal year.

data.title: M Vest Water lifts revenues and deepens NORWAFLOC® footprint despite Middle East delay
data.description:
M Vest Water AS ( (DE:7YA) ) has issued an announcement.

M Vest Water reported first-half 2026 revenues of NOK 15.7 million, with Q2 sales of NOK 9.9 million, a 27% year-on-year increase driven by strong chemical sales and higher NORWAFLOC® volumes. Chemical revenues in the second quarter rose 36% from a year earlier, underscoring momentum in core product demand across aquaculture and industrial water treatment.

Aquaculture has emerged as a profitable standalone segment with strong earnings visibility, supported by the company’s largest salmon slaughterhouse customer ramping consumption of NORWAFLOC® in the second half of 2026. The company is targeting annual turnover of NOK 100–150 million from aquaculture between 2028 and 2030, signaling an ambition to scale this vertical significantly within its overall growth strategy.

Operationally, M Vest Water advanced its technology footprint by completing two deliveries of sensor-driven systems that help salmon processors meet new EU regulatory requirements while maintaining high treatment efficiency. These implementations strengthen its value proposition as regulations tighten and highlight the potential for recurring revenues from integrated solutions across slaughterhouses.

The company also achieved a key milestone at METHA, one of Europe’s largest dredging plants, where a long-term pilot showed NORWAFLOC® improves treatment performance and operational efficiency, paving the way for commercial negotiations. The firm’s portfolio includes proprietary chemicals such as NORWAFLOC®, which are used in aquaculture, dredging, and industrial wastewater facilities.
